# edgeos_static_interface_route (Resource)

A static IPv4 route out of an interface without a gateway address (`protocols static interface-route <prefix>`), for point-to-point links such as WireGuard, OpenVPN or PPPoE.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "edgeos_static_interface_route" "site_b" {
  destination = "10.66.0.0/24"

  next_hop_interfaces = {
    wg0 = {
      description = "site to site tunnel"
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `destination` (String) Destination network in CIDR notation, such as `198.51.100.0/24` or `0.0.0.0/0` for a default route. It must be the network address (no host bits). Changing it creates a new route.
- `next_hop_interfaces` (Attributes Map) Interfaces to send the traffic out of, keyed by interface name such as `wg0`. Use `{}` for an interface without options. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--next_hop_interfaces))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The destination prefix.

<a id="nestedatt--next_hop_interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `next_hop_interfaces`

Optional:

- `description` (String) Free text description.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Keep the interface route in the config but switch it off (the `disable` node). Defaults to `false`.
- `distance` (Number) Administrative distance from 1 to 255. Lower wins when several routes match the same prefix. Unset uses the EdgeOS default of 1.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import edgeos_static_interface_route.example '10.66.0.0/24'
```
